question: How much will Nasdaq-100 Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: all 10-trading-day windows of Nasdaq-100 minus S&P 500 price return since 2015, which centers near +0.25pp (NDX excess ~5-7pp/yr, 7 of last 10 calendar years); 2026 YTD (QQQ +17.0% vs SPY +12.9% through Sep 4) implies almost exactly the same per-window drift, so the prior and the current year agree. Futures price returns add a small structural tilt to NQ because ES gives up ~2x the dividend yield and late-Sep/early-Oct is dividend-heavy for SPX (a few bp). Against that: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% with >50% odds of another October hike, the 10Y is ~5%, and oil above $100 favors SPX's ~4% energy weight that NDX lacks - and NDX's ~1.1 beta means any macro-driven selloff (hot PCE, hot Oct 2 payrolls) hits it harder. I therefore keep the median only marginally above zero at +0.25 rather than extrapolating last week's tech-led bounce. Dispersion is the dominant feature: implied index correlation is near one-year lows (COR3M 11.58) with DSPX at 32.91 and VXN/VIX at 1.29, and the window contains PCE, quarter-end, Micron's FQ4 print after the close Sep 30, and September payrolls on the resolution day itself - so I use the full implied-vol-derived width rather than narrowing. Slight left skew (tech drawdowns are sharper than melt-ups) puts p10 marginally further from the median than p90. Escape mass ~1% each side: a >5pp move in 10 sessions is ~3.5 SD but has real precedent (DeepSeek Jan-2025, the Apr-2025 tariff shock), with named mechanisms in both directions. No human market prices this spread - Kalshi/Polymarket/Manifold have only outright index level or daily up/down contracts - so there is no crowd anchor and I stay near the reference class.

calls.reconciliation: The three runs were already tightly clustered (medians +0.20/+0.25/+0.32, widths 3.4/3.78/3.8), so reconciliation was about checking their factual substrate rather than splitting numbers. (1) Apparent momentum disagreement - Runs 1-2 cited NDX's +4.5pp YTD lead and last week's tech leadership, Run 3 cited NDX lagging SPX by 3.3pp quarter-to-date since Jun 29. Not a contradiction: NDX built the lead in H1 and gave part back in Q3. Both are real, they point opposite ways, and neither survives as a large tilt on a 10-session horizon. (2) Base rate - Run 2 (weekly ^NDX/^GSPC closes, overlapping) and Run 3 (FRED daily, consecutive non-overlapping) computed this independently from different data and landed on +0.23 median and +0.21 mean/+0.14 median respectively; Run 1's long-run drift argument agrees. Settled at ~+0.2, which I adopt. (3) Dispersion - the live judgment dispute. Run 1 argued for the full implied width citing COR3M near one-year lows (11.58) and DSPX 32.91; Run 2 argued VIX at 14.81 and a cooling recent weekly SD (0.83-1.13pp) justify trimming below the 4.7pp overlapping-sample width that the spring 2026 AI melt-up inflates. Both have a point, and three methods (realized biweekly SD 1.54, daily SD 0.467 x sqrt(10) = 1.48, implied 1.2-1.5) bracket SD at 1.45-1.55. I take 1.45 -> 3.7pp width, slightly inside Runs 2-3 because the overlapping-window sample genuinely overstates dispersion and current vol is low, but above Run 1's 3.4 because the window is unusually event-dense. (4) Minor factual - Run 1's 'VIX 15.44 on Sep 18' is the Sep 17 close; Run 2's 14.81 is Sep 18. Immaterial. Sources also conflicted on the Sep 14-18 weekly Nasdaq gain (+2.6% vs +0.7% Composite) and on Sep 17-vs-18 day attribution of the NDX +1.73% session; I could not settle this without web access, so I let the 'NDX led last week' claim carry reduced weight rather than treating the larger figure as established. (5) Market check - all three searched Polymarket, Kalshi and Manifold independently and all found only index-LEVEL or daily up/down contracts (KXNASDAQDUD, KXNASDAQ100Y, KXINXY, Polymarket SPX close Dec 2026), none matching this question's quantity, window or resolution source. Concordant 'none found'; no blend. (6) Escape mass - the three priced 1.0-1.5% per side against a ~3.4-sigma threshold, i.e. deliberately fat-tailed versus normal. I keep ~1.2% per side, marginally heavier low, since the named mechanisms (rate/duration purge, AI-capex scare) are the sharper ones and NDX carries the higher beta. Final: median +0.22, width 3.7, left-skewed - inside the members' range because the reconciled evidence genuinely puts it there, not as a compromise.
